summary: On the platform Marta mistakes the yellow ticket validator for a machine needed by every ticket. Her rigid monthly chip card will not fit. With a short clarification she rescues her card, gives the machine an amused farewell and safely puts the chip card away.
cliffhanger: Next time, Marta returns home and faces the separate recycling bins.
visual_hook: Marta firmly trying to push a rigid plastic card into the thin paper slit of a yellow platform stamping box.
everyday_problem: Newcomers often mistake regional transit validators as mandatory for all tickets, risking damage to plastic chip cards or mobile phones.
practical_resolution: Marta learns that her already-valid monthly chip card needs no mechanical stamping, takes the card away from the validator and safely stores it herself.
marta_goal: Validate her new transit ticket correctly before boarding the train.
marta_decision: Pull the plastic chip card safely away from the narrow slot and put it in her jacket pocket ready for ticket inspection.
visual_payoff: Marta protectively hugs her intact chip card, raises one eyebrow at the stamping machine as if declining its invitation, and confidently slips the card into her wallet.

creative_review.previous_weakness_addressed: Remove three repeated closing shots and finish a complete nine-shot story; retain eight already-generated matching scenes to avoid wasting quota.
creative_review.visible_comic_action: Marta treats the stamping machine like an overenthusiastic host, protects her chip card with a playful eyebrow reaction and puts it away herself.
creative_review.next_experiment: In the next fresh episode, replace repeated clarification questions with two visibly different prop actions and a payoff that works even with the sound muted.
